body:
During the Ryza explosion, I have seen some people think Atelier was more adult oriented. People see the porn and expect more from the games than there is, and the horny crowd the porn led in furthered that reputation. Then there's stuff like the 'sexual content' tag that's on Steam (which is user voted, but someone new can't know it's a meme tag). So, yes, the character herself is hot (I personally quite appreciate her and Klaudia both), but the game not as much as people might be led to believe.

As for where this is coming from: a lot of people come to Atelier for wholesome experiences, so I tell them what matches that more. Contrary to their expectations, Ryza is rather wholesome. Meanwhile Arland, contrary to its own reputation, is not all wholesome (it's mild as far as anime goes), and there are definitely people who get angry about its content. This is not the majority, but the people who are sensitive to these things appreciate the heads up.

Hope you enjoy Arland!

body: Howdy, I just wanted to say thank you. Barrel Wisdom has been the website to use when I've gone through Sophie's trilogy and Ryza's, so you just having this page is greatly appreciated.

I grew up with a DS and no home consoles, so Annie was actually my first Atelier game.  Looking back at it for what it is, in my opinion it is worthy of some discussion, if not on the level of the rest of the series.  As a game on weaker hardware, it's interesting to puzzle out what was intended design vs what was a design limitation.  Interestingly, though you primarily interact with the world through small, walkable environments, they all take up exactly one screen - no scrolling.  Gathering consists of mashing the 'A' button to collect resources from designated spots, with RNG playing a huge role.  The light business-sim component is a really neat diversion from the series' core mechanics.  However, some of the requirements for the True Ending are downright brutal with the time limit given, and it's easy to get locked out of things if you go in unaware.

"...Most of the time. Check your duplication/reduction costs before committing."

This is definitely true for weapons/armor. I tried adding Ultra Purity to a piece of armor. Duplication cost was 20k while reduction was around 9k.

body:
"You wanna start with Yumia? Start with Yumia" is actually advice I would *not* proffer to newcomers to the franchise. The crafting system, relative to any other Atelier game, is so far removed from any others than it can barely be called such. The crafting and synthesis is the defining feature of the games around which all else is built; Yumia has essentially ripped out the core of what makes an Atelier game an Atelier game, because the crafting system is so simplified and streamlined that it's essentially been destroyed. It's by far the weakest entry and it's not representative of what Atelier is supposed to be. By suggesting Yumia to someone who's never played Atelier, there's a pretty elevated risk of said newcomer distinctly getting the wrong impression about what Atelier is, which could be bad twice over: first they may think that Atelier is "just another" JRPG franchise and be turned off if that isn't what they're looking for, *or* they think "hey this is my jam!" and then play another Atelier game and be turned off by the crafting emphasis.

Have you played it? I would be pretty worried about someone getting the wrong idea about Atelier if Yumia is their first impression and would suggest literally anything else.

body: I'm pretty sure that Ryza got a localization adjustment at some point between this guide and your comment that changed certain words like "Lord" to "Master" and several other things.
A fully charged swing with the Scythe Axe on one of the trees in Limewick Hill gives you 35k gems worth of materials if you prefer chopping trees instead of doing alchemy.

Sad to say being a Gacha game means you need to make money. And for me I never spent any of it and enjoyed the story, usually logging on once a day to knock off all the grinding. Was pretty excited about the new training option even if I couldn't auto-clear it right away. And then the game says it's ending service, here's your pity gems if you bought a pass, have a great day. Suppose people outside JP just weren't spending enough money for them to justify translation costs. Atelier stories was never about the cash though, excluding the literal money endings in some.
